sections.h2: Which Marshall County, KY offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter, and two of them share a building. The Property Valuation Administrator and the County Clerk both list 1101 Main Street in Benton, while the Sheriff's Office collects the bill and runs the online lookup.

  • The PVA sets assessed values and takes exemption applications. The county directory shows weekday hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm and 270-527-4767 as an alternate phone.
  • The County Clerk records land documents for the whole county and, according to the county's own description, collects delinquent property taxes. Call 270-527-4740. The clerk's office is open for in-person business on weekdays from 8 AM to 4:30 PM.
  • The Sheriff's Office collects county taxes, and the county website links to its property tax bill lookup and payments page.

If your house lies inside Benton, there is a second bill. The City of Benton collects its own property tax at 1009 Main Street, 270-527-8677, and its website warns residents not to use the city's payment link for county taxes.

sections.h2: What makes Marshall County a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Marshall County is a lake county at the western end of Kentucky, and the water is the main fact about its real estate. Of 340 square miles, 39 are water, about 11 percent. The Tennessee River and Kentucky Lake form the northeastern boundary, and the county is the only one in the Purchase region that does not touch another state.

The Kentucky legislature created the county in 1842 from the northern half of Calloway County. Farming dominated until the 1940s, when the Tennessee Valley Authority built Kentucky Lake. The lake brought fishing resorts and tourism, and cheap power from Kentucky Dam drew chemical and manufacturing plants to the Calvert City area. Impoundment also flooded the towns of Birmingham and Gilbertsville, and Gilbertsville was rebuilt west of its first site.

Benton is the seat and largest city. Calvert City and Hardin are the other incorporated cities, and Gilbertsville is a census-designated place. Unincorporated communities include Aurora, Draffenville, Fairdealing and Briensburg. Part of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge lies in the county. Marshall County sits in the Central time zone, so confirm which clock applies when you schedule a closing with an out-of-county buyer or lender.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Marshall County homes?
sections.html:
Marshall County skews older, with 25.1 percent of residents aged 65 or older, and owner occupancy is high.

sections.h2: How were Marshall County's 2026 tax bills scheduled?
sections.html:
Marshall County's 2026 bills went out late. The Marshall County Sheriff's Office announced that collection would begin November 1 because tax rates had to be finalized before the bills could be printed and mailed.

  • November 1 to November 30, 2026: 2% discount
  • December 1 to December 31, 2026: face amount
  • January 1 to January 31, 2027: 5% penalty
  • February 1 to April 15, 2027: 10% penalty

That pattern follows the alternative schedule in KRS 134.015(3), which the Department of Revenue may set when billing is delayed. In a normal year the discount deadline is November 1, face amount runs through December 31, and penalties start in January. The Department of Revenue says unpaid bills are transferred to the county clerk at the close of the cycle and then pick up interest of 1 percent per month.

Each year, read the dates printed on the bill itself. A seller whose bill has not come should call the Sheriff's Office promptly.

sections.h2: What can a Marshall County owner do about a high assessment?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA for a conference before or during the inspection period. The PVA must describe how your value was reached and write down what each side said, as KRS 133.120 provides.

The next stage is a short written petition filed with the Marshall County Clerk by one workday after the inspection period closes, naming the parcel, the reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. The county board of assessment appeals then holds a hearing, generally 25 to 35 days after inspection ends under KRS 133.030.

  1. Gather sales of nearby houses, an appraisal, insurance records or building costs.
  2. Appear yourself or send a representative with written authorization.
  3. Pay on the value you claim while you wait. No appeal delays collection.

A taxpayer who skips the county board cannot go straight to the state Board of Tax Appeals, so do not let the petition deadline pass. A Marshall County owner whose land is farmed should also ask whether the acreage is valued by agricultural use rather than by market price, a rule the Department of Revenue ties to Section 172A of the state constitution.

sections.h2: Do older Marshall County homeowners get a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, and with a quarter of the county aged 65 or older, many owners are eligible. The exemption is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, deducted from the assessed value of a home that is the owner's permanent residence.

At the county's median value of $173,800, the taxable figure would be $124,700. The application goes to the Marshall County PVA with proof of age, such as a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability applicants need a federal or retirement-system classification of total disability. Annual renewals are required for most disability filers, but not for service-connected veterans or people ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. The exemption follows the owner, so a buyer who qualifies must file a new application.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax lien and the deed when a Marshall County house sells?
sections.html:
A delinquency lien stays on the parcel for up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), no matter who holds title, so any bill still open at closing has to be cleared. Because the clerk collects delinquent property taxes in Marshall County, a payoff for last year's bill comes from the clerk's office at 270-527-4740, while the current bill is paid to the sheriff.

The deed is recorded with the same clerk. The grantor owes a transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value, rounded up, under KRS 142.050, and the clerk collects it before recording. A sale at $173,800 would owe $174. The clerk's homepage also promotes a program to guard owners against deed theft. Ask the office how to enroll in it before you sell or after you close.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Marshall County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the property tax bill lookup linked from the Marshall County Sheriff's page on the county website. The sheriff's office collects the bill, and the PVA answers valuation questions.

faqs.q: Does Benton charge its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Benton collects city property tax separately, and its website says city payments and Marshall County payments must not be mixed. City Hall is at 1009 Main Street, 270-527-8677.

faqs.q: What was the Marshall County discount for 2026 bills?
faqs.a: It was 2 percent for payments made November 1 through November 30, 2026, under the schedule the Sheriff's Office announced. Face amount applied in December 2026, followed by a 5 percent penalty in January 2027.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent taxes in Marshall County?
faqs.a: The County Clerk does. Once the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid bills move to the clerk at 1101 Main Street in Benton, and interest of 1 percent per month starts to accrue.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Marshall County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and apply through the Marshall County PVA.
